paragraphs: R. Yaakov, Rav Naḥman's father. In the first chapter of Bava Metzia (16b), Rav Naḥman said: 'Father was one of Master Shemuel's judicial scribes.' Yuḥasin follows Tosafot's approach: it is Rav Naḥman without further designation who said his father was a scribe, and Rav Naḥman without further designation is bar Yaakov (see his entry). Yet nearby Yuḥasin writes that Rav Yitzḥak, Rav Naḥman's father, was Master Shemuel's scribe; that follows Rashi's view that Rav Naḥman without further designation is bar Yitzḥak. He thus awards the deed to two parties!
